title: Nigeria's constitution vests legislative power of the federation in a National Assembly of a Senate and a House of Representatives
summary: Nigeria's constitution vests legislative power of the federation in a National Assembly of a Senate and a House of Representatives.
body: The English text vests the legislative powers of the Federal Republic in a National Assembly consisting of a Senate and a House of Representatives, with power to make laws for the peace, order, and good government of the Federation. The source says: "Powers of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 4 The legislative powers of the Federal Republic of Nigeria shall be vested in a National Assembly for the Federation, which shall consist of a Senate and a House of Representatives." The vesting is federal. State legislative power is a different part of the constitution and is not this sentence.
